key.name: xiaomi-user-id
key.summary: Mi Home account the login in the keyring belongs to
key.description: Written by the preferences window after a login or a logout, so the shell knows to read the keyring again. Empty when no one is logged in.

key.name: view
key.summary: How the devices are laid out
key.description: "tabs" shows one room at a time with the rooms as tabs above two columns of tiles, "grid" puts small tiles three to a row, "rooms" lists every room under its own heading, "control" groups the devices into modules like a control centre.

key.name: type-colors
key.description: Each kind of device gets a colour of its own. When off, everything uses the accent colour.

key.name: room
key.description: The lowercased room name, "@other" for devices in no room, or empty for all rooms.

key.name: panel-sensors
key.summary: Devices whose readings show in the top bar
key.description: Mi Home device ids, in the order they are shown next to the icon.

key.name: panel-interval
key.description: How often the sensors shown in the top bar are read while the session is unlocked. Opening the menu reads everything at once as well.

key.name: pinned
key.description: Mi Home device ids. Pinned devices come first in every view and have a tab of their own.

key.name: order
key.description: Mi Home device ids in the order the user arranged them. Devices not in the list follow, switches first, then by name.

key.name: hidden
key.description: Mi Home device ids left out of the menu.

key.name: folded-groups
key.description: Groups that show only their title. On the Devices page: find, top-bar, mihome, gree, tapo, cast, tv, sonoff and ewelink; on the Accounts page the same sources with "accounts-" in front.

key.name: names
key.description: Mi Home device ids mapped to the name the user gave them here. Mi Home itself keeps its own names.

key.name: icons
key.description: Device ids mapped to the icon of their tile: the name of one of Nook's own glyphs, or the absolute path of an image copied into Nook's data folder.

key.name: extra-tiles
key.summary: Switches with a tile of their own
key.description: Each entry is "device id/service id/property id/property name", a switch inside a device that the user put on a tile next to it, like a gateway's guard mode.

key.name: groups
key.description: Device ids mapped to the name of the group they were dragged into. Each group shows as one module.

key.name: gree-units
key.description: A JSON list of the units bound in the preferences: mac, ip, name, key, cipher and version. The key is what a unit hands out to anyone on the local network who asks, so it is kept here and not in the keyring.

key.name: find-skipped
key.summary: Devices left out of Search Everything
key.description: Ids like tapo:uuid or gree:mac of devices the user removed. Search Everything on the Devices page does not add them back; a device's own Search or its switch in Find Devices does.

key.name: tapo-cameras
key.description: A JSON list of the cameras found on the local network: id (the camera's own uuid), ip, name, model and xaddr (its ONVIF device service; port 2020 is Tapo). The logins they are watched with are kept in the keyring, not here.

key.name: cast-speakers
key.description: A JSON list of the speakers found in the preferences: id, name, model, ip and port. Nothing secret; a speaker answers anyone on the local network.

key.name: tvs
key.description: A JSON list of the TVs added in the preferences: id, brand, name, model, ip and mac. What a TV hands out when it is paired is kept in the keyring, not here.

key.name: sonoff-switches
key.description: A JSON list of the Sonoff switches in DIY mode found in the preferences: id, name, ip, port, and outlets for one with several channels. Nothing secret; in DIY mode a switch answers anyone on the local network.

key.name: ewelink-devices
key.description: A JSON list of the eWeLink devices added in the preferences: id, name, model, uiid, outlets and room. Nothing secret; the eWeLink login stays in the keyring.

key.name: ewelink-region
key.description: The region of the eWeLink account, or empty when logged out. Written by the preferences on login and logout to tell the shell; the login itself is in the keyring.

key.name: hue-bridges
key.description: A JSON list of the Hue bridges added in the preferences: id, name, model, ip and the fingerprint of the certificate seen when the bridge was added. The key a bridge hands out when paired is kept in the keyring, not here.

key.name: hue-devices
key.description: A JSON list of the lights, plugs and sensors read from the Hue bridges: id, bridge, kind, name, room, model and what each can do.

key.name: hass-server
key.description: The address of the Home Assistant server, or empty when not connected. Written by the preferences to tell the shell; the access token is in the keyring.

key.name: hass-devices
key.description: A JSON list of the devices read from Home Assistant: the entity behind each, its type, name, room and the entities of the same device shown with it, with the attributes the card is built from.

key.name: homekit-accessories
key.description: A JSON list of the HomeKit accessories paired in the preferences: id, name, model, ip, port, and the services and characteristics of each accessory behind it. The keys made at pairing are kept in the keyring, not here.

key.name: smartlife-user
key.description: The id of the Smart Life account, or empty when logged out. Written by the preferences on login and logout to tell the shell; the login itself is in the keyring.

key.name: smartlife-devices
key.description: A JSON list of the devices read from the Smart Life account: id, name, room, category, model, channel, and the data points Nook shows with their limits.

key.name: colored-icon
key.description: Draws the logo in cream with a clay doorway; off, it is monochrome in the colour of the other icons in the top bar.

key.name: hidden-rooms
key.description: Rooms whose tab the menu leaves out, by lowercased room name, plus "@pinned" and "@other" for the Pinned and Other tabs. Their devices stay under All.

key.name: alerts
key.description: Mi Home device ids of sensors behind a Xiaomi gateway, mapped to whether their events become notifications. A sensor not in here notifies if it is a leak, smoke or gas sensor and stays quiet otherwise.

key.name: sensor-rules
key.description: JSON: Mi Home device ids of sensors behind a Xiaomi gateway, each mapped to its own thresholds. "openFor" is the minutes a door may stay open; "warm", "cold", "wet" and "dry" are the temperature in degrees and the humidity in percent to tell of crossing; "battery" false keeps a low battery quiet.

key.name: location
key.description: "panel" gives Nook a button of its own in the top bar; "quick-settings" makes it a tile in Quick Settings, with the logo and the readings among the system icons.

key.name: panel-box
key.summary: Part of the top bar the button is in
key.description: The left, centre or right part of the top bar. Not used when Nook is in Quick Settings.

key.name: panel-index
key.summary: Place of the button in that part
key.description: Counted from the left of the part of the top bar the button is in; zero puts it first.

key.name: middle-click
key.summary: What a middle click on the button does
key.description: "refresh" looks for the devices again, the way the button in the menu does; "settings" opens the preferences.

key.name: prefs-target
key.description: Written by the shell just before it opens the preferences: the id of a group on the Accounts page, such as "accounts-tapo", optionally followed by a space and a device. The window scrolls there and clears the key.

key.name: hover-switch
key.summary: Pointing at another top bar button opens its menu
key.description: The usual top bar behaviour: while Nook is open, moving the pointer onto another button closes Nook and opens that button's menu. When off, Nook stays open until a click outside it.
